## Summary

Second vertical slice of the G8 resource HUD: bounds and the loss-bearing marker. A bounded key prints `value / max`; a key at its maximum and at its minimum each carry a printed state marker as well as a colour cue; a declared irreversible key prints `irreversible` beside it (colour is secondary), matching GDD §3.4.3.

## Target outcome

A designer's authored caps and the never-restored subset are legible in the HUD from plain data, and every state is signalled without relying on colour.

## Acceptance Criteria

- A bounded key renders its declared maximum alongside the current value (for example `Morale 5 / 8`); a key at its declared maximum and a key at its declared minimum are each distinguishable by a **printed** channel as well as any colour cue.
- A key in the declared irreversible / loss-bearing subset is marked by a **printed** channel (the word `irreversible`, or an equivalent glyph with accompanying text) beside the key as well as by colour, matching the "Irreversible key" row of GDD §3.4.3.
- Bounds and irreversibility are supplied as plain data (the caller's `bounds` / `irreversible` records) and render correctly for arbitrary key sets, not only the five GDD keys.
- An unbounded key renders no `value / max`, and a key outside the irreversible subset renders no irreversible marker.
- Headless unit tests cover the `value / max` display, the at-maximum printed marker, the at-minimum printed marker and the irreversible printed + colour marker.

## Minimal implementation

1. Extend `ResourceHud` rendering with a per-key `value / max` text when `bounds[key]` exists.
2. Add printed at-maximum / at-minimum state markers plus a secondary colour tint (the printed channel is primary).
3. Add the printed `irreversible` marker beside a key in the `irreversible` set, with the §3.4.3 secondary colour cue.
4. Extend `tests/ui/resourceHud.test.ts` for max display, both printed state markers, the irreversible marker and the no-marker cases (test-first inside the slice).

## Key Files

- `src/ui/ResourceHud.ts`
- `tests/ui/resourceHud.test.ts`

## Dependencies

- Child 1 (declared-set rendering) — the markers extend the same per-key items.

## Deliverables

- Bounded-key display and printed at-maximum / at-minimum markers.
- Printed irreversible marker with a secondary colour cue.
- Headless unit tests for both.

## Impact

A player can read a capped key as "value / cap" and see, in print rather than colour alone, when a key is full, empty, or a one-way loss.

## Summary

Third vertical slice: the HUD's value-update path. `setResources(bag)` re-renders values, animating the change and playing at most one shared SFX on the animated path and snapping silently under reduced motion; `destroy()` is idempotent.

## Target outcome

A scene can push a new resource bag after every choice and get an audible/animated change in normal play, an instant silent change under reduced motion, and no crash when no audio is wired.

## Acceptance Criteria

- A value update (`setResources(bag)` or equivalent): under reduced motion (the caller-resolved `getEffectiveReducedMotion()` flag) snaps to the new value with no tween and plays **no** SFX; otherwise it animates the change and plays at most one `COMMON_SFX_KEYS` SFX per update through the injected `SoundManager`, and is a silent no-op when no `SoundManager` is supplied.
- `setResources` animates only the value change, never re-flows the layout, and reports the new bag through the optional observability `onChange` hook.
- `destroy()` is idempotent and removes every tracked listener, tween and per-key text object; a post-destroy `setResources` is a safe no-op.
- Unit tests for the component (headless, mocked Phaser) cover: label / order / value rendering from a resource bag; bound display and the at-maximum and at-minimum printed markers; the irreversible printed + colour marker; a value change that spilled or clamped; the reduced-motion instant, silent path; exactly one SFX on an animated update; and idempotent `destroy()`.

## Minimal implementation

1. Add `setResources(bag)`: diff values, update texts, run a short tween/pop on changed values.
2. Branch on `reducedMotion`: snap with no tween and no SFX; otherwise call `soundManager.play(sfx)` once per update when a manager and a `COMMON_SFX_KEYS` key are supplied.
3. Add the `onChange` invocation and idempotent `destroyContent()` teardown (tweens + texts).
4. Extend `tests/ui/resourceHud.test.ts` with fake tween stubs: animated update → one SFX; reduced motion → no tween and no SFX; no manager → silent no-op; spilled/clamped resulting values render; double `destroy()` is safe (test-first inside the slice).

## Key Files

- `src/ui/ResourceHud.ts`
- `tests/ui/resourceHud.test.ts`

## Dependencies

- Child 1 (render contract).
- Child 2 (bound/irreversible markers) — the spilled/clamped and marker assertions build on the rendered items.

## Deliverables

- `setResources` update path with reduced-motion and SFX behaviour.
- Idempotent `destroy()` with full teardown.
- Headless unit tests for the update path.

## Impact

A player sees the economy change animate and hear it land after every choice, or get the same new value instantly and silently when they prefer reduced motion — so a resource change is never missed and never startling.

## Summary

Fourth vertical slice: adopt `ResourceHud` in `GymLongErasureScene` at the `statusBar.resources` SLL anchor, replacing the bespoke `resourcesText` / `resourcesLine` / `resourceLabel` status path while keeping the scene's observable behaviour green.

## Target outcome

The in-repo five-key economy renders through the shared component — declared keys, labels, bounds and the irreversible subset from the committed manifest — and the Gym browser suite still proves the same starting resources, per-choice changes and layout anchor.

## Acceptance Criteria

- `GymLongErasureScene` renders its `statusBar.resources` surface through the new component (declared keys, display labels, irreversible set and bounds from the committed `long-erasure-episode.json`; values from the resource projection's `getResources`) instead of the bespoke `resourcesLine` / `resourceLabel`, and keeps its existing observable behaviour (starting resources, per-choice resource changes, layout anchor) green in the browser suite.
- The component is constructed at the SLL-resolved `statusBar.resources` anchor with right alignment; no literal coordinate is introduced, and the bespoke status renderer (`resourcesText`, `resourcesLine`, `resourceLabel`) is removed.
- The epilogue's "Left when the timeline closed" summary reuses the same derived labels map (it does not re-implement the HUD), and the scene passes `bounds` / `irreversible` from `LONG_ERASURE_EPISODE_MANIFEST` rather than a copied literal.
- `tests/gym/GymLongErasureScene.browser.test.ts` stays green; assertions are extended only where needed to observe the component's rendered text/markers. Scene help-text and Gym-index documentation changes are handed to the documentation slice (`CG-0MWZ9WD9P003IAQM`) rather than duplicated here.

## Minimal implementation

1. Construct `ResourceHud` in `buildChrome()` at the resolved `statusBar.resources` point with `declaredKeys` from the content, `labels` from a derived label map, `bounds` / `irreversible` from the manifest, and the run's resource bag.
2. Call `setResources` from `render()`; delete `resourcesText`, `resourcesLine` and `resourceLabel`.
3. Keep the epilogue line by formatting it from the same labels map.
4. Run the Gym browser suite; extend the HUD assertions only if the rendered text/markers need direct observation.

## Key Files

- `docs/gym/GYM_INDEX.md`

- Child 3 (update path).

## Deliverables

- Gym Long Erasure HUD rendered by the shared component at the SLL anchor.
- Bespoke status-line helpers removed; browser suite green with the adopted component.

# Presentation helper: presentSceneExit()

**Summary:** The Phaser-based `presentSceneExit()` function that renders an act/scene banner from `{ actTitle, sceneTitle, outcome, route }`, positions every element from injected SLL anchors (a `sceneBanner` zone), sequences the steps (title → outcome → route), and returns a promise that resolves on dismissal.

## Acceptance Criteria
1. Renders text objects for `actTitle`, `sceneTitle`, `outcome`, and `route` — each positioned from the provided SLL `resolveAnchor` callback, never absolute pixel coordinates.
2. Sequences steps in order: act/scene title → outcome → route — with configurable dwell times (`stepMs`).
3. The outcome displays the word (`success` / `partial` / `failure`) as primary text, with optional colour tint as secondary cue only.
4. Dismisses on click/key press (`skipOnInput`), showing all text instantly without further animation.
5. Auto-advances after `autoAdvanceMs` (default configurable, default 3000ms).
6. Returns a `SceneExitPresentationHandle` with `{ skip(), destroy(), promise, readonly plan, readonly done, readonly destroyed }`.
7. Does not move the camera — a documented note says `runSceneTransition` (or the game) owns the camera fade/slide.
8. **Covers parent AC 0.** A new shared helper `presentSceneExit()` in `src/ui/scene-exit-presentation.ts` (exported from the `@ui` barrel) renders an act/scene banner from `{ actTitle, sceneTitle, outcome, route }`, positions **every** element from injected SLL anchors (a `sceneBanner` zone: `actTitle`, `sceneTitle`, `outcome`, `route`) — never an absolute pixel coordinate — and returns a promise that resolves once when the banner is dismissed.
9. **Covers parent AC 2.** The outcome is colour-independent: the banner prints the outcome word (`success` / `partial` / `failure`) as its primary channel, with tint only as a secondary cue; a test asserts the word is present in each outcome state.
10. **Covers parent AC 6.** The presentation can be layered on the existing camera transition without either double-playing motion: the helper does not itself move the camera, and a documented note says `runSceneTransition` (or the game) owns the camera fade/slide.

## Minimal Implementation
- `src/ui/scene-exit-presentation.ts`: `presentSceneExit()` + `SceneExitPresentationHandle` type.
- SFX played via injected `SoundManager` with key from `resolveSceneExitSfxKey()`.
- `tests/ui/scene-exit-presentation.browser.test.ts`: Phaser browser test asserting banner renders, sequences steps, dismisses on input.

## Deliverables
- Working code, tests and docs for this slice, committed and green.

## Dependencies
- CG-0MWZCKY1W008JV83
- CG-0MWZCLIBF000SU2U

## Key Files
- `src/ui/scene-exit-presentation.ts`
- `tests/ui/scene-exit-presentation.browser.test.ts`

# Reduced-motion instant presentation

**Summary:** When reduced motion is enabled (either via the explicit `reducedMotion: true` flag or `getEffectiveReducedMotion()`), `presentSceneExit()` presents all information synchronously in one step — no tween, no timer, no SFX — and still resolves the promise.

## Acceptance Criteria
1. With reduced motion, the banner renders all four fields (act title, scene title, outcome word, route) immediately in one step.

6. **Covers parent AC 3.** Reduced motion (explicit `reducedMotion` flag or `getEffectiveReducedMotion()`) presents the same information synchronously in one step — no tween, no timer, no SFX — and still resolves the promise; a test asserts the instant state contains the act title, scene title, outcome word and route.

# Idempotent teardown and lifecycle

**Summary:** `presentSceneExit()` teardown must be total and idempotent: `destroy()` (and scene `shutdown`) removes the timer, tween, every input listener, and every created game object — leaving no orphans and allowing re-invocation.

## Acceptance Criteria
1. `destroy()` removes all timers, tweens, input listeners and game objects created by the helper.
2. Calling `destroy()` multiple times is idempotent — no errors, no double-cleanup side effects.
3. Calling `skip()` after `destroy()` is a no-op (does not throw).
4. The handle exposes `readonly destroyed: boolean` reflecting lifecycle state.
5. After `destroy()`, the promise has resolved and the `done` flag is `true`.
6. Browser test asserts no orphaned game objects remain in the scene after teardown.
7. **Covers parent AC 5.** Dismissal and teardown are total and idempotent: a click/key skips to the end (full information, no further tween), an auto-advance dismisses after a configurable dwell (`autoAdvanceMs`), and `destroy()`/scene `shutdown` removes the timer, tween, every input listener and every created game object, leaving no orphans; tests assert idempotence and no residue.

## Minimal Implementation
- `src/ui/scene-exit-presentation.ts`: `destroy()` implementation with cleanup list (objects array, timer, listener refs).
- `tests/ui/scene-exit-presentation.browser.test.ts`: teardown assertions.

## Deliverables
- Working code, tests and docs for this slice, committed and green.

## Dependencies
- CG-0MWZCM6I0005DYZ6

## Key Files
- `src/ui/scene-exit-presentation.ts`
- `tests/ui/scene-exit-presentation.browser.test.ts`

Implementation notes (value-update slice)
- `setResources(bag)` diffs the declared keys against the rendered items and rewrites only the text of items whose value changed. Item positions and the container position are never recomputed, so the row does not re-flow (a width change from one digit is accepted, no re-layout).
- Animated path: one tween whose `targets` are the changed texts (pop scale 1.15 → 1, 240 ms, Quad.easeOut) plus **at most one** SFX per update through `soundManager.play(sfx)`; the SFX key is the caller's `COMMON_SFX_KEYS` choice. Missing manager or missing `sfx` is a silent no-op.
- Reduced motion: no tween, no SFX, text snaps; `setReducedMotion()` also stops an in-flight pop and resets scale so a live settings toggle takes effect.
- `onChange` fires once with the new declared-key snapshot only when a value actually changed (both paths); identical-bag updates do nothing.
- `destroy()` (UIComponentBase) stops and forgets every tracked tween before destroying texts/container; a post-destroy `setResources` returns early (no text write, tween, SFX or callback).
- Marker words and colour cues are re-resolved on update, so a value reaching a bound prints `full`/`empty` and a spilled/clamped figure prints exactly as supplied.
- Tests: `tests/ui/resourceHud.test.ts` extended to 68 headless cases (mock tween + mock SoundManager seams). Unit suite: 296 files / 5144 tests green; `npm run build` green.
